title: Write the use-by date on a food container's label with a marker
instruction: Write the use-by date 11/22 on the container's label.
context: Date marking prepared food is routine in every commercial kitchen: the FDA Food Code (3-501.17) requires ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food held more than 24 hours to be marked with the day by which it must be used or discarded (at most 7 days). O*NET lists the work among the tasks of restaurant cooks ("keeping track of old and new items, and rotating stock"), short-order cooks ("stamp the time and date on food in coolers") and baristas ("Wrap, label, or date food items"); restaurant, institution and short-order cooks total about 2.0 million US workers (BLS, May 2025). Most kitchens write it by hand with a permanent marker on masking tape on the container's side. The robot must hold a light container steady, pick up a marker and write a short date legibly on a curved, tapered surface, pressing the tip with handwriting force (about 1 N) along each stroke and lifting it between strokes, then put the marker down. The instruction states only the goal.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). Arms start in the ready pose. Container: Bare by Solo DM32R-0090 32 oz round deli container, clear recycled PET, 8.81 cm across the bottom, 11.71 cm across the top, 14.5 cm tall, holding about 470 ml of room-temperature tap water (filled until container, water and lid weigh 500 g on a kitchen scale), its recessed lid pressed on and sealed with a strip of masking tape around the rim; centre at x 30, y 0, on a taped outline. Label: a strip of Scotch 2050 masking tape, 48 mm wide, about 10.5 cm long, around the side facing the right arm (front right), 5.1 to 9.9 cm above the table, blank. Marker: black Sharpie Fine Point (30001), cap off, 12.3 cm long, 11 mm barrel, lying along x, tip forward, its middle at x 20, y -17, on a sheet of 20 lb copy paper (US letter, 27.9 x 21.6 cm, long side along x, centred under the marker, taped to the table at its corners) that keeps ink off the table. The grippers hold the marker only by its barrel, away from the tip (the demo grips it 6 cm behind the tip), so the pads never touch the ink; each finger pad is also wrapped in one layer of the same masking tape, replaced if inked. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: A person reads the label after the trial. 0 if the container was tipped over or pushed more than 3 cm off its outline, if more than 2 cm of line went on the container off the tape, or if more than a fifth of the ink on the tape belongs to no character. Otherwise each character of the date gets credit = strokes drawn / its strokes. Strokes: 0 one (the oval; plain or slashed); 1 one (the upright; a flag or a base may be added, not counted); 2 two (hook with diagonal, base line; round or flat top, with or without a small loop at the bottom); 3 two (upper and lower bowl); 4 three (diagonal, or upright of an open-top 4; crossbar; upright); 5 three (top bar, short upright, bowl); 6 two (stem, curved or straight; loop); 7 two (top bar, diagonal; a cross bar may be added, not counted); 8 two (upper and lower loop); 9 two (loop; stem, curved or straight); / one. A stroke is drawn when at least 80% of its length is inked (its gaps, measured with a ruler, add up to 20% or less). A character gets 0 if it reads as another character, or if more than a quarter of its ink is off its strokes (scribbled over). Score = 0.8 x the mean credit over the characters, + 0.2 if every character has all its strokes and reads as itself and the marker lies on the table or paper, let go. Handwriting is read as written: characters 2.4 to 3.6 cm tall, anywhere on the tape, upright or slanted up to about 25 degrees either way, narrower or wider, evenly or unevenly spaced, count. 1.0 = success (held 1 s).
reset_notes: Replace the tape strip with a blank one at the same height (5.1 to 9.9 cm); container on its outline with the strip facing the right arm, lid taped shut, 500 g in all (top up the water if needed); marker on the paper on its outline, cap off; replace the paper sheet, and the tape on the finger pads, if they have ink on them.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes (container side: 40 facets); the water is part of one rigid 0.5 kg body (no sloshing). Ink emulated: a 1 mm dot every 0.5 mm where PhysX reports the nib (within 3 mm of the tip) touching the container with a normal force of at least 0.5 N (low end of handwriting force, README); harder presses also ink; no line-width or ink-flow model. The reader is an automatic stroke match standing in for a person reading the label, checked on independently drawn handwriting (README).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,600 steps; the arms stay near their bases and never reach the marker, no ink); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,319 of 1,600 steps)
